name: properties-continuation-split-name
why: Properties continuation can split the credential name so the visible line is not a direct name=value pair.

name: ini-section-credential
why: INI files often put secrets under a credential-named section with generic value keys.

name: hocon-object-secret-section
why: HOCON object nesting can put the credential concept in a parent key and the secret under a generic child.

name: terraform-variable-default
why: Terraform variable blocks may name the variable as secret while the actual value is under default.

name: k8s-stringdata-generic-key
why: Kubernetes stringData often stores sensitive values under app-specific keys that are not credential names.
input:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: app
stringData:
  djangoSettings: CorrectHorse9!

name: k8s-data-base64-generic-key
why: (was held only) Kubernetes Secret data values are base64 and may sit under arbitrary keys.
input:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
data:
  config.yml: {{B64 40}}

name: systemd-envfile-reference
why: systemd unit files may carry secrets in ExecStart arguments rather than simple assignments.

name: ansible-vault-inline
why: (was held only) Ansible vault encrypted blobs are secret material but not necessarily matched as credential assignments.

name: sql-insert-password-column
why: SQL INSERT columns can name a password separately from the VALUES tuple.

name: sql-copy-table
why: SQL COPY dumps put credential column headers on one line and data values on following rows.

name: saml-attribute-value
why: SAML/XML attributes can hold secrets in AttributeValue with credential meaning in a Name attribute.

name: xml-attr-secret-parent
why: XML can put credential context in an element name and the actual secret in a generic attribute.

name: xml-signature-keyinfo
why: (was held only) XML signatures can include sensitive key material inside KeyInfo children not named private_key.

name: html-table-password-column
why: HTML tables can put Password in a header and the value in a following cell.

name: markdown-table-password-column
why: Markdown tables can carry secret semantics in column headers rather than key-value syntax.

name: windows-unc-userinfo
why: Windows UNC-style resource strings can embed credentials outside URL syntax.

name: powershell-securestring-plaintext
why: PowerShell SecureString commands can contain cleartext values as positional arguments.

name: prose-creds-colon-pair
why: Prose credential shorthand may use user:password without a URL scheme.
input: The creds are alice:CorrectHorse9! for staging.

name: prose-possessive-pw
why: Possessive shorthand can evade exact natural-language patterns.
input: the pw's CorrectHorse9!, don't paste it anywhere public

name: multiline-name-separator-value
why: Credential name, separator, and value can be split across separate lines with no continuation marker.

name: csv-quoted-multiline-cell
why: CSV quoted cells can span lines and carry secret values under a header.

name: url-query-token-generic-path
why: URLs can carry credential query parameters without known token prefixes.

name: cookie-inside-set-cookie-comma
why: Cookie values can appear inside combined header blobs with commas and attributes.

name: never-send-normalization-ligature
why: (was held only) Compatibility characters can hide never-send terms if only simple folding is used.
input: The oﬃce deployment passphrase is CorrectHorse9!

name: never-send-greek-homoglyph
why: Greek homoglyphs in never-send terms can evade ASCII-only term matching.

name: toml-array-of-tables
why: TOML arrays of tables can put secret semantics in table names and generic fields.

name: python-dict-tuple-pair
why: Python config may use tuples of key/value pairs rather than assignments.

name: cpp-designated-init
why: (was held only) C++ designated initializers can use credential field names with dot syntax.

name: pem-json-escaped-no-footer
why: (was held only) JSON-escaped PEM-like material may use escaped newlines and omit a footer.
